All articles

Guides for buying, selling and caring for crystals.

How to spot real amethystBuying guide

Look for colour that varies inside the stone, with lighter and darker zones. Glass fakes are often uniform and have tiny round bubbles. Natural pieces also feel cool and slightly heavy for their size.

Starting a crystal shop on a small budgetFor resellers

Begin with five or six stones that sell easily, such as rose quartz, clear quartz and amethyst. Buy small mixed lots, see what moves, and then move the best sellers into larger orders.

Cleaning and caring for your crystalsCare

Wipe most stones with a soft dry cloth. Keep selenite away from water, since it dissolves, and store softer stones apart from hard ones so they do not scratch.

What to check before a bulk order of rose quartzBuying guide

Check that the colour is even across the lot, and look for cracks and cloudy patches. Ask for a sample from the same batch so the pieces you receive match the ones you approved.

How to pack crystals for shippingFor resellers

Wrap each piece in bubble wrap and keep points from touching each other. Fill any gaps so nothing moves, and use a second outer box for clusters and lamps.

Natural or dyed quartz: how to tellBuying guide

Dyed stones often look too bright and show colour pooling in cracks. If a price looks very low for a vivid colour, ask the seller whether the stone is natural.

Crystals that sell best at fairs and eventsFor resellers

Small, low-priced pieces move fastest: tumbled stones in little bags, rose quartz hearts and bracelets. They are easy for buyers to carry and easy for you to restock.

Choosing stones for a gift boxIdeas

Pair one larger stone with two or three small tumbled stones. Keep the sizes the same across every box so each customer gets an equal set.

Why crystal prices differBuying guide

Price depends on the stone, its size and clarity, how it is cut or polished, and its weight. Large, clear, unchipped pieces cost more than small or cloudy ones.
